# A Whole Course: Navigation and Onboarding

Use when the user provides a semester's collection of materials, asks for a course overview or wants saved maps reused. A question about how two lectures connect is [Cross-lecture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ningzhanglab/Econ-Agent-Skills/main/link/econ-learn/tasks/cross-lecture.md). A focused question about an available slide never needs onboarding first.

## Defaults

- **Indexes:** none is mandatory. A Course Map, Lecture Index, Notation Registry, Homework Map, Figure Index or Course State is made only when it helps the task or the user asks.
- **Depth during onboarding:** inventory and map, not deep commentary on every page.
- **Saved files:** only when requested, as [Deliver a file](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ningzhanglab/Econ-Agent-Skills/main/link/econ-learn/tasks/deliver-file.md) describes: the verified course's `Agent Outputs/`, private, never a public repository.

## Two different orders

Keep the **instructor's sequence** (syllabus first, then slide numbering and titles; filenames and upload order are weak evidence) apart from the **conceptual prerequisite order** you infer. Label inferred dependencies, and never present the inferred order as what the lecturer taught.

## Onboarding

1. List only the files actually accessible, with their role (lecture, syllabus, homework, solution, reading, code). Group same-basename `.tex`/PDF/Word files in one course folder as one logical document; tell real variants apart by evidence ([Sources and versions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ningzhanglab/Econ-Agent-Skills/main/link/econ-learn/guides/sources-and-versions.md)).
2. Take the course identity and order from the syllabus. Without one, build a provisional order and say it is provisional.
3. Make only the indexes that help, from their templates: [Course Map](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ningzhanglab/Econ-Agent-Skills/main/link/econ-learn/templates/course-map.md), [Lecture Index](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ningzhanglab/Econ-Agent-Skills/main/link/econ-learn/templates/lecture-index.md), [Figure Index](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ningzhanglab/Econ-Agent-Skills/main/link/econ-learn/templates/figure-index.md) (the [inventory helper](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ningzhanglab/Econ-Agent-Skills/main/skills/econ-learn/scripts/inventory_tex_figures.py) finds TeX figure references; a reference is not a figure seen), [Notation Registry](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ningzhanglab/Econ-Agent-Skills/main/link/econ-learn/templates/notation-registry.md) (only symbols actually observed, scoped by lecture: the same symbol in another lecture may mean something else), [Homework Map](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ningzhanglab/Econ-Agent-Skills/main/link/econ-learn/templates/homework-map.md) and a [Course State](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ningzhanglab/Econ-Agent-Skills/main/skills/econ-learn/templates/course-state.example.json) when a persistent checkpoint is requested.
4. Label each cross-lecture link *explicit*, *derived* or *provisional*, as in [Cross-lecture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ningzhanglab/Econ-Agent-Skills/main/link/econ-learn/tasks/cross-lecture.md).
5. For a large collection, work in passes as [Large files](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ningzhanglab/Econ-Agent-Skills/main/link/econ-learn/guides/large-files.md) describes.
6. Close with what is confirmed and what is provisional: order, coverage, missing sources and figures, and the next study step.

## Progressive verification states

Use these in maps and indexes:

- **DISCOVERED:** the file exists; contents not examined.
- **INDEXED:** mapped well enough to locate topics, not read page by page.
- **REVIEWED:** text, equations and figures inspected for a stated range.
- **BLOCKED:** inaccessible, corrupt, too large or missing a dependency.

A lecture can be INDEXED overall with some pages REVIEWED. Never mark a lecture REVIEWED from a sample. When a source is revised, downgrade the affected entries until they are rechecked.

## Answering from saved maps

A map, index or Course State is navigation, not evidence. Use it to find the slide, then reopen the original and its neighboring assumptions before any equation or figure claim. If a source changed since the map was saved, invalidate only the affected entries and say so.

## Which source wins

Slides and lecture notes define what was taught; the syllabus defines the official order. Homework and solutions show applications, not the lecture's notation. Outside textbooks and papers deepen the interpretation but never overwrite the course's model or symbols.

Never claim to understand the whole course when only filenames, headings or sampled pages were read.
